correctness.rationale: The graph has 24 permutations and degree three. Explicit lexicographic-neighbor enumeration computes all 2^24 updates; an independent Cartesian-isomorphic 12+12 parity factorization computes complete 4096-state P and Q maps and an exact formula for first recurrence. Both return fixed=208, period-two states=43056 and all six entry-depth bins with maximum five; witnessed by initial bitmask 9762. A complete group of 48 spatial automorphisms is constructed and checked edge by edge; period-orbit phase quotient and orbit-size weighted sums are verified. The minimum nonuniform fixed support follows from matching-cut equivalence and six commuting-square cosets. No larger or infinite-domain conclusion is inferred.

evidence: Goles–Olivos assert eventual periods at most two for symmetric thresholds; no exact graph census. Benjamini et al. discuss finite graph period-two property and prove infinite/random-graph results. Kaaser et al. prove general voting-time bounds, with no particular truncated-octahedral case. Collares et al. study a monotone infection rule, not nonmonotone synchronous voting.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General period-at-most-two coverage does not settle the exact sharp entry time, state populations, geometric orbit sizes, or square-face supports. The permutahedron bootstrap result uses a different, irreversible local rule and cannot imply nonmonotone voting recurrence.

value.rationale: A full labelled temporal and symmetry classification on the canonical 24-vertex cubic Archimedean graph is a natural exact dynamical invariant. The sharp five-update clock and strong oscillatory basin predominance are mathematically informative and not implied by general eventual-period-two theory. The six size-four square-face stable supports give a motivated geometric boundary, and the 12+12 bipartite reduction provides a reusable structural verification method. This is a finite self-contained classification, not a claim of a general new network theorem.
